messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: 502/504 spike at API edge detected. Error rate 18% over last 2m on /v1/generate. Paging maya (oncall) and eng-runtime team.

maya: Ack, I'm on it. Quick summary pls — is this global or regional?

ajay: Seeing the spike from 03:20Z. Primarily hitting edge-proxy instances in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. 5xx ratio up to 22% on the gateway layer. Latency also climbing to 1.8s p50 -> p95 6s.

sasha: Noted — we pushed proxy config rollout 5m ago (traffic-fanout gating change). Rolling window on the rollout shows a correlation with the spike. Commit: `git rev: 9a3f2b4` config key `fanout.max_parallel=80 -> 200`.

leo: CDN logs look clean, cache hit ratio unchanged. This looks internal to edge-proxy -> backend fanout. Backpressure from backends might cause 502 from proxy when upstream closed connections.

ops-runner: Reverting the config is fastest mitigation. I can flip the rollout to previous revision. Do we want full revert or targeted region?

maya: Targeted revert to us-west-2 first. If that reduces error rate, escalate to global. Also need a customer-impact quick list. support-desk can you pull top affected orgs?

support-desk: Pulling now — initial query shows 6 orgs with >10% 5xx of their requests, 24 orgs with >1%. Large few are SaaSCo and EduPortal. Will DM billing+AE.

ajay: Snippet from edge-proxy logs (sensitive redacted):
```
[03:21:12] edge-proxy-az3: upstream_http_502: backend_service=aks-gen-1 conn_reset by peer after fanout to 32 targets
[03:21:13] edge-proxy-az3: upstream_timeout (504) waiting for response from model-worker (p95 response > 8s)
```

maya: OK, ops-runner proceed with regional revert. Also enable route-level fallback to 'stable-pool' for /v1/generate for affected regions. Put a short notice to API users status page if impact persists.

ops-runner: Running revert command: `infractl proxy-rollout rollback --region us-west-2 --to-rev 9a3f1c0`

incident-bot: Action logged: rollback requested by ops-runner at 03:23Z.

ajay: After revert start: error rate in us-west-2 dipped from 22% -> 9% within 45s. p95 latency reduced to 2.1s. eu-west still elevated at ~18%.

sasha: Reverting eu-west now as well. Also we should cap fanout concurrency at 64 instead of full revert for long term. The change was intended to improve latency but apparently exposed unstable backends.

ops-runner: Revert eu-west-1: `infractl proxy-rollout rollback --region eu-west-1 --to-rev 9a3f1c0` — applied.

incident-bot: Status update: rollback complete for us-west-2 and eu-west-1 at 03:25Z. Error rate globally trending down.

ajay: Customer impact: SaaSCo experienced API failures for ~6m window, estimated ~2.3% of their total requests failed. No PII involved.

maya: Good triage. Next steps: 1) keep rollbacks in place until we validate backend worker stability; 2) create an ops runbook entry for fanout guardrails; 3) open an RCA ticket for proxy config and model-worker capacity.

sasha: I'll own the RCA. Immediate patch: set `fanout.max_parallel=64` and add a soft circuit-breaker that returns 429 when backend queue depth > threshold.

leo: Also suggest a temporary client-side retry budget change to avoid retry storms: set per-client max retries=1 for 10m. Ops-runner can we push that?

ops-runner: Pushing retry-budget policy: `infractl policy apply retry-budget --set per_client=1 --ttl 10m`. Applied at 03:29Z.

support-desk: Notified affected customers via status page update draft. Sending targeted emails to top 6 impacted orgs.

maya: Preparing handoff to devex + eng-runtime for post-mortem. Oncall shift ends in 40m — I'll remain reachable for escalation. Handoff to sasha for RCA and follow-ups.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: primary responder maya -> sasha at 03:35Z. Incident severity downgraded to SEV-2; monitoring until stable.

ajay: Quick note for logs team: add `fanout_concurrency` sampling to request traces for next 24h to gather telemetry.

sasha: Will open the RCA ticket (ENG-RCA-4921) and schedule postmortem. Thanks team.

maya: Great work, everyone. Closing live triage. If any regression, re-open this thread. :thumbsup:
